report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a specific, interpretable difference: Model B (B − A) has stronger activations that correspond to cooking/culinary/recipe vocabulary and concepts than Model A.

Why I believe this
- Token-level signals: Across many of the highest-norm cells (particularly layers 18–25 and also visible earlier around 16–22), the logit-lens top tokens are consistently culinary words: "Cooking", "Cook", "kitchen", "Kitchen", "Bake", "Baked", "Bake", "butter", "Butter", "cake", "cakes", "Chef", "chefs", "recipes", "baking", "culinary", "Thanksgiving", "Bake", "Showcase", etc. This pattern is repeated across many layers and positions.
- Layer/position localization: The L2-norm of the difference is concentrated in the deeper layers (large jumps from ~layer 14 onward, peaking layers 23–25) and primarily at early token positions (pos0 and pos1). That indicates the difference is a strong prior-like or early-context effect in later transformer layers (i.e., B more strongly encodes signals that project to culinary vocabulary early in the sequence).
- Consistency across cells: The same semantic cluster (cooking/recipes/baking) appears repeatedly in many of the top cells rather than a few isolated tokens, supporting a substantive domain-level difference rather than noise or idiosyncratic token artifacts.

Caveats / what I am not claiming
- I am not claiming a specific training objective or exact dataset change — only that the activation difference corresponds to cooking/culinary lexical/conceptual content. The mechanism could be a dataset-distribution difference, a domain-specific fine-tune, or some other change that increases culinary priors in B.
- Some other tokens appear in a few cells (e.g., landscape, names, digits), but they are far less frequent and not the dominant pattern.

Short statement: Model B shows a clear, concentrated increase (relative to A) in activations that map to cooking/baking/culinary vocabulary and concepts, especially in deep layers at the first one–two token positions, consistent with B having stronger culinary/recipe-like priors.
